This study investigates the differential cross sections of angular $\alpha$-particle production in the $^{6}$Li+$^{51}$V interaction across an energy spectrum from 2.14 MeV to 11.6 MeV. Experimental data are analyzed using two models: the Double-folding Wave function Amplitude Summation (DFWAS) and the Geometrical Optically-Modified Double-folding Approximation with Pauli Blocking (GOMDFPB). In the DFWAS approach, reactions proceed via $\alpha$-substructure formation through $p$-stripping and subsequent elastic scattering mediated by the sum of the one-body neutron and folding-derived two-body effective optical potentials. The GOMDFPB method utilizes a double-folding potential derived from $^{6}$Li+$^{51}$V, modified by a geometric form factor to account for Pauli blocking effects in the optical model. Results indicate that the DFWAS model offers superior agreement with experimental $\alpha$-production trends, providing a more physically rigorous explanation compared to GOMDFPB with geometric modifications.

This paper presents a new robotic climbing strategy grounded in an updated biomechanical model of gecko adhesion. While Pacific lampreys are renowned for their adhesive capabilities, this study reveals that their proposed toe-press climbing mechanism is mechanically unviable. We propose an alternative "toe-shear" mechanism that functions effectively for vertical surfaces with an inclination up to 90 degrees and surfaces as smooth as those simulated for gecko feet. Implementing this "lamprey climbing" algorithm on a 1-kg, four-toed robot equipped with variable anisotropic adhesion demonstrated successful vertical ascent at a velocity of 0.14 m/s.

This paper introduces a novel, data-informed methodology for crafting optimal personalized anti-cancer therapies. We begin by formulating a mathematical model of the body's immune response to colon carcinoma, grounded in a Fokker-Planck framework that tracks the evolution of immune cell distributions. Utilizing an adjoint-based optimization algorithm, we determine the most effective drug regimens to induce desired immune dynamics, with results demonstrating significant potential for clinical application.

This study addresses the D2D scheduling challenge within a network of $K$ users, aiming to maximize scheduling throughput while minimizing the Average Age of Information (AoI) for each. To achieve this, we introduce DL-based Scheduling (DLS), an innovative DL-driven method that operates on channel state information (CSI) to boost throughput and age efficiency. The DLS framework employs a neural network to map CSI into an output layer, where each element represents the probability of scheduling a specific user. This paper offers a rigorous mathematical analysis of DLS, demonstrating that it achieves the theoretical lower bound of CSI utilization variance. Additionally, we derive an upper bound on the mean CSI values, which serves as a cap for average AoI. The results indicate that DLS significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in both throughput and age efficiency.

This paper establishes the preservation of total helicity as an integral of motion within ideal fluid dynamics. By representing ideal fluids through symmetric, compressible Euler equations, and defining total helicity as the volume integral of the specific vorticity–specific relative velocity contraction, we analytically validate that this quantity remains constant over time. Notably, this validation accommodates initial data exhibiting polynomial decay of arbitrary order.

Building on the work presented in \cite{KochTzvetkov2013} regarding Klein-Gordon equations, we establish optimal growth estimates for the $k\to\infty$ limit of the reflection coefficient for the damped linear Davey-Stewartson II system. This analysis covers both cases where the potential is confined and where it extends non-compactly, utilizing an approach grounded in Riemann-Hilbert theory alongside Green's identity techniques.

Post-Newtonian (PN) theory predicts that compact binaries with eccentric detection-threshold eccentricity ($e \sim 0.2$) will develop significant eccentricity ($>0.1$) as they evolve. This paper provides precise calculations of eccentricity evolution using up to 3.5PN accuracy, covering both adiabatic changes and finite timescale regimes. We further examine the impact of the 4PN adiabatic correction on this process. By employing evolutionary models for star formation and mergers, we determine eccentricity distributions for merging compact objects within our galaxy and nearby cosmic volumes. Our findings indicate that eccentricities in these populations can easily surpass 0.1, a level sufficient to alter gravitational-wave phase and amplitude by over 10 percent.

The x-ray free-electron linear oscillator (XFELO) is a proposed device for generating highly coherent, tunable x-ray light via lasing. Although its core physics are well-understood, engineering challenges have delayed experimental validation. This paper proposes using an XFELO to seed a undulator-based coherent x-ray amplifier (XALAS), a strategy that should resolve current limitations and simultaneously validate the XFOLO's functionality. We provide a design for such an amplifier operating in the soft x-ray spectrum, focusing on an energy range of 2 to 5 keV. By employing a 5 GeV accelerator, we estimate that an XFELO could amplify seed pulses from the 2 to 5 keV range to energies between 50 and 1250 microjoules. Consequently, the resulting amplified signal would achieve peak powers exceeding 50 gigawatts and brightness levels surpassing $10^{33}$ photons per second per 0.1 per eLA.

Event detection is a fundamental task in graph analysis with broad applications, ranging from identifying community changes and graph clustering to tracking concept evolution. While existing solutions are often task-specific, there is currently no unified methodological framework to address the graph event detection problem. This paper introduces **EVDEG**, the first unified methodology for detecting graphs that undergo events. The system constructs a detection pipeline comprising four key components: (i) defining event categories, (ii) formulating event representations, (iii) representing the input graphs, and (iv) establishing event detection tasks. By leveraging this unified pipeline, the authors identify and analyze various existing solutions, resulting in the creation of **GoWeGD**, the first comprehensive benchmark for event detection on dynamic graphs.

This study examines the resolution of an astrophysically motivated initial value problem featuring an imploding shock interface at rest within density-gradient media. The analysis utilizes the self-similar variables proposed by Zel'dovich and Kolmogorov, transforming the governing equations into autonomous forms. By solving these equations numerically, we characterize the end-state shock structure for various power-law exponent values. Additionally, the investigation explores the link between specific heat ratios and achievable admissible densities, particularly within the near-shock limit, and outlines self-similar fractional transformations enabling the conversion of one valid solution into another.

In the domain of Artificial Intelligence, specifically within Machine Learning and Deep Learning models, the absence of explainability remains a significant drawback. While AI systems generate predictions based on intricate algorithms and vast datasets, they offer no insight into the reasoning behind those outcomes. As AI permeates critical sectors like healthcare and automotive, accountability in decision-making has become paramount, driving the integration of Explainable AI (XAI). Although XAI focuses heavily on technical aspects, existing approaches neglect the perspectives of end-users, thereby restricting user-centric accountability for decisions. This study introduces a novel, user-focused methodology for gathering necessity to support XAI initiatives. Leveraging literature reviews and insights from stakeholder experts, we developed this user-centered approach to ensure decisions made by AI are transparent to those most affected by them.

The identification and removal of colorectal polyps is vital for preventing colorectal cancer, as excising them prevents the formation and spread of the disease. During colonoscopy procedures, polyps appear as distinct protrusions on the bowel wall; if left untreated, they can evolve into cancer. To support clinical practice, we introduce the UniToPatho dataset, which comprises 1,111 histopathological images of colorectal polyps. Acquired through the digital scanning of stained tissue sections, these images feature precise annotations for cells, structures, and tissues at both organ and microscopic levels. Specifically, the dataset includes images categorized into polyps with no dysplasia and those with dysplasia, along with labeled sub-images to support binary classification tasks. Furthermore, polyps with dysplasia are segmented into mild, moderate, and severe categories based on visual characteristics. We also provide detailed segmentation masks for various anatomical elements, including the lamina propria, tumor cells, tumor glands, and background areas. To facilitate cutting-edge research, we release this comprehensive resource along with detailed metadata and evaluation scripts.

This paper examines information leakage from a noiseless source to a deterministic encoder under the constraint of zero error probability. The extent of such leakage is quantified using the minimum conditional entropy, also known as the min-entropy. Building upon prior research, this study adopts a graph-theoretic methodology to investigate fundamental properties related to minimal conditional entropy for constrained systems. Key contributions include: (1) establishing upper and lower bounds on information leakage; (2) determining the precise conditions required to achieve these leakage bounds; (3) proving that, with the possible exception of two cases, the information leakage value is always an integer; and (4) analyzing specific coding scenarios, particularly focusing on generalized Sinsmeyer's alphabet. The latter analysis involves representing codes as subgraphs of Cartesian graph products and utilizes concepts such as the maximum average subgraph degree and the maximum average order of a graph to characterize optimal code properties.

Deep generative models have proven effective across various inverse problem applications. This study introduces a hierarchical architecture, designated as MrSARP, leveraging deep generative techniques specifically for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image super-resolution. The proposed method employs two sequential stages: first, it utilizes a convolutional neural network to upsample low-resolution inputs to an intermediate resolution, followed by a deep generative model that refines these images to the final target resolution. This intermediate step is designed to mitigate generation difficulties and enhance convergence stability. SAR datasets were utilized to evaluate the approach, with results demonstrating superior performance against current state-of-the-art methods regarding both quantitative metrics and qualitative analysis. Furthermore, the architecture's versatility suggests potential adaptation for other restoration tasks within the domain of image processing.

The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) represents a hybrid quantum-classical approach to solving combinatorial challenges. Its efficacy relies heavily on the performance of a classical optimizer tasked with refining the parameters of the QAOA quantum state. We introduce a Bayesian framework for these classical optimization steps, utilizing class probabilities to direct parameter updates. By applying this method to several benchmark problems, we observed that it matches the performance of existing techniques while requiring significantly fewer circuit executions. Furthermore, the results indicate that this algorithm excels in scenarios where evaluating circuit circuits is expensive.

This work examines q-learning within continuous-time Markov decision processes featuring finite state and action spaces. Under the assumption of ergodic system dynamics, we establish the existence and uniqueness of unique fixed points for both average-cost and per-cost (or discount) variants of continuous-time q-learning. Additionally, by introducing a small $\epsilon$-perturbation to the system states, we demonstrate the $\epsilon$-optimality of the corresponding Q-optimal policies. In the section concerning the q-average cost, we prove that under certain conditions, the limit of continuous-time q-learning converges to the solution of its discrete-time counterpart. As an application, this theoretical framework is used to derive q-Learning from the foundational $\epsilon$-perturbation approach originally developed by A. R. Weiss.

We investigate the low-energy magnetic excitations of half-filled electrons moving on a connected system of two triangular sublattices with alternating bond strengths. By employing a Hubbard model, we analyze various interaction and geometry scenarios. At half-filling, all considered cases exhibit a bond-ordered valence solid (VO) ground state. Magnetic spin waves are found to be damped by electron-hole pair creation near the K point, except along specific lines where the quadratic dispersion remains linear. Notably, the VO state can transform into a spin-triplet state—either an incommensurate or antiferromagnetic order—due to electronic correlations, a mechanism known as order-by-disorder. We identify a parameter range where the lowest energy corresponds to finite-q spin order, a region that expands further with the application of a magnetic field.

This paper presents a novel approach for vertebra localization and identification in computed tomography (CT) images. Our method leverages the anatomical structure of the spine to enhance performance, specifically introducing a convolutional neural network to localize the spine and a specific data-driven loss function that enforces anatomically constrained smoothing during this process. Additionally, we developed a further constraint-based optimization step to identify the vertebrae, ensuring they adhere to spinal anatomy. By utilizing spine rectification and anatomically constrained optimization, our technique achieves superior performance on the LiSSiM dataset compared to previous state-of-the-art approaches, reaching a mean accuracy of 96.1%.

Within the framework of stochastic thermodynamics, electric currents are modeled as Markov chains that accept a discrete time step $\tau$ as a fundamental unit. These trajectories encompass all current paths occurring over the interval $[0, T]$ where the total duration satisfies $T/\tau$ being an integer. We demonstrate that as the system progresses to the limit of continuous time ($\tau \to 0$ at a fixed $T$), the distribution of these trajectories converges weakly to a well-specified limiting distribution. This finding extends previously to a broader class of semimarkovian processes than standard Markovian assumptions. Furthermore, we show that the moments of this trajectory distribution yield valid upper and lower bounds for the corresponding moments calculated strictly within continuous-time models. We examine several physical kinetic schemes to confirm the significant physical relevance of the fluctuation effects; specifically, the moments may either suppress or amplify those observed in continuous-time theories. Additionally, we reveal a fundamental constraint: the variance in this domain cannot fall below the limit set by the net charge fluctuation.

This research investigates the behavior of relative quantum cohomology under birational transformations, specifically focusing on the behaviorally nice case. We analyze how the perturbation of Floer theory for the boundary divisor operates within this framework. Additionally, we establish the consistency of the (relative) gluing technique and the (relative) wall-crossing process. Notably, we demonstrate that the (perturbed) mutation rule for variation gluing applies across the (relative) mutation and gluing concepts (both the and the relative concepts apply here).

This study introduces an innovative approach to acoustic wave control, featuring the near-total transmission of such waves between two piezoelectric crystals positioned in close proximity. When a wave enters the first crystal, a coupled acoustic resonance forms within the system, resulting in the wave's transfer to the second crystal, where it emerges fully transmitted. This mechanism, which operates as a tunable resonator, permits precise manipulation of the transmission amplitude. Furthermore, transmission becomes strictly off when the incident wave's frequency aligns with the system's resonance gap, effectively suppressing the wave. Consequently, this method provides a novel framework for the precise manipulation of acoustic energies.

This study introduces an all-optical room-temperature platform that replicates fundamental linear optical reservoir theories using exciton-polariton condensates. By leveraging the unique capabilities of our system, we demonstrate the practical realization of various optical reservoirs, offering significant potential for integrating and deploying reservoir quantum optics at practical temperatures with straightforward experimental methods.

The discovery of the ultra-hot gas giant K2-22 b in 2020 sparked excitement due to its anomalous atmospheric composition, which lacks water vapor. This study investigates the planet's atmosphere using high-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy obtained with the Gran Telescopio Canarias and the Integral Field Unit on the Low Resolution Atacama, which revealed a dense shroud of dust particles in the lower atmosphere. The dust particles are estimated to have radii between 1.5 and 2.0 Earth radii, with a volume mixing ratio of hydrogen to hydrogen of approximately $10^{-3}$, which is consistent with a high mass loss rate of $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-5}$ Earth radii per year. The presence of dust and the associated mass loss are attributed to silicate clouds, which are consistent with predictions for highly irradiated environments. "This analysis examines an isolated singularity $f \in \mathbb{C}[z_0,\dots,z_n]$, where $[n \ge 2]$, focusing on the relationship between the geometry of the singular variety and the topology of its Milnor fiber. Specifically, we demonstrate that if $\text{dim}(\text{Crit}(f))=1$, then the fiber's boundary—topologically structured as an $[n-1]$-cell complex—exhibits simple connectivity on its components. This finding establishes that a fiber component's boundary is nullhomotopic, implying a structure where each part behaves nicely within the complex. As a direct consequence, assuming $\text{dim}(\text{Crit}(f))=1$, any generic transversal line section through the singularity yields a fiber with an isolated point as its only boundary component, thereby confirming the separation of variables phenomenon. Furthermore, our approach provides a streamlined, self-contained demonstration of the original proof by Milnor and Morin regarding fibers' normal smoothness and separation variables

Daany is a C# library designed to streamline data analysis for .NET developers. It offers functionality comparable to Pandas for reading and writing CSV files in dataframes, performing filtering and grouping operations, joining dataframes, and executing various other pandas-style tasks. This capability extends to performing advanced statistical calculations such as mean, median, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum. Although the initial release focuses primarily on dataframe operations, future updates plan to incorporate Series-specific features and support for other data structures like graphs and tables.

Although widely regarded as a quintessential figure of the Scientific Revolution, Galileo's legacy is frequently misunderstood. This chapter seeks to correct the historical record by emphasizing that, for Galileo, mathematics held supreme importance, a stance that inherently meant the secondary status of philosophical inquiry. This perspective is illustrated by his famous dismissal of Aristotle's mechanics, a rejection that stemmed not from a lack of knowledge but from his conviction that such old theories were needless because the mathematical models offered superior clarity. Consequently, this focus on quantitative precision often led to a neglect of conceptual depth, a strategy that served the Scientific Revolution well in the short term but created long-standing challenges for subsequent generations.

Recombination in the early universe is a pivotal phase that determines the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). While the Saha equation is frequently employed to model this process, its neglect of photon diffusion and photo-ionization renders it inaccurate regarding photon polarization spectra. This study implements a novel non-Gaussian framework for photon spectra that accommodates both photo-ionization and diffusion, contrasting these results with those from the Gaussian approximation and the Saha-based method. Our simulation of the recombination epoch demonstrates that the Saha equation fails to capture non-Gaussian effects on photon spectra, which are instead more comprehensively modeled by the Gaussian approach. Additionally, we examine the impact of these spectral non-Gaussianities on the CMB's power spectrum, finding that their contribution is negligible.

This paper describes a hybrid simulation employing an adaptively coupled 1D-PIC model within MHD frameworks to analyze magnetic island merger dynamics. In regions where islands converge, this localized PIC component calculates Landau kinetic effects, while the global MHD system provides surrounding boundary conditions. Our findings indicate that, unlike standard MHD predictions, these regions of enhanced island collision support the growth of secondary islands. This phenomenon arises specifically because the embedded PIC domain captures velocity-distribution anisotropies that generate instability-driving free energy.

This document outlines the design and development of Ammanueis, a tool intended to assist developers by managing routine programming tasks. Its primary objective is to elevate developer productivity by granting access to their past experiences, thereby freeing them from mundane work. By having this common chores managed through the "magic comment" #pragma suggest, which triggers an AI model, users can focus their energy on innovative and more fulfilling aspects of their job.
